operations.name: T. Luesse

expected.charges: Resisting the eviction of a Black family in Indianapolis.
expected.sentence: One year at the Indiana State Penal Farm and a $500 fine; held beyond the prison term to work off the fine at $1 per day. Entered the farm on May 25, 1931, and was released on March 3, 1933.

operations.research_note: Daily Worker May 9, 1932, page4, Nat Boss, Indiana Plans a Second State Hunger March, explicitly dates sentence May22 following May1931 hunger march. Corroboration June1,1932 Daily Worker says year served May22; Indiana History Bureau cites Kokomo Tribune May23,1931 sentence report. Farm entry May25 preserved separately; no arrest date inferred.
